title: Applied ML experiment scratchpad — 2026-03-11 (Jordan Lee)
content:
Date: 2026-03-11
Owner: Jordan Lee
Context: quick scratchpad for the week — evaluating 4-bit quantization (PTQ/QAT) impact on instruction-following quality for the 7B family. Follow-ups from Monday sync (Asha) and tickets JIRA-ML-412/JIRA-ML-419.

Goal:
- Short: measure downstream instruction-following and factuality regression from 4-bit quant on subset of production prompts.
- Long: pick a quant config that yields >=0.98 relative perf on safety/QA prompts while reducing token cost by ~2x.

Hypothesis:
- PTQ (GPTQ-like) with per-channel quant + outlier clipping will preserve most quality for short instructions, but will degrade long-context factuality.
- QAT on small calibration dataset (2K steps) will recover ~1-2% absolute accuracy on QA metrics.

Experiment setup (notes):
- Base model: redwood/opt-7b-v2-checkpoint (float16 baseline)
- Variants: PTQ-4bit (gptq-perchannel), PTQ-4bit+act-order, QAT-4bit (2k steps lr=3e-5), Int8 baseline for comparison
- Eval set: 1) prod-instr-sample-1k (mixed short instructions) 2) prod-qa-200 (long context QA) 3) safety-check-100
- Metric suite: RAG-acc (exact match where applicable), Rouge-L, Distinct-1, toxicity-flag rate (internal classifier), latency (p50/p95) on p4d-16xlarge instance
- Prompting: use current prod prompt template v3 (see linked PR)

Commands (local notes):
- convert: scripts/quant/convert_gptq --model redwood/opt-7b-v2 --bits 4 --per-channel --clip 3.0 --out ./runs/ptq-4c-clip3
- qat: scripts/quant/run_qat.py --model ... --steps 2000 --lr 3e-5 --out ./runs/qat-4b-2k
- eval: tools/eval_runner --model ./runs/... --prompts datasets/prod-instr-sample-1k.jsonl --metrics all --output ./evals/2026-03-11/

Quick results (first-pass, 2026-03-11 15:10 UTC):
- Float16 baseline (opt-7b-v2): prod-instr-sample-1k: EM 0.72, Rouge-L 0.61, latency p50 120ms/p95 240ms
- PTQ-4c-clip3: EM 0.70 (-2.8%), Rouge-L 0.59 (-3.3%), latency p50 95ms/p95 210ms (cost ~1.9x improvement)
- PTQ-4c-clip3 + act-order: EM 0.705 (-2.1%), Rouge-L 0.595 (-2.6%)
- QAT-4b-2k: EM 0.715 (-0.7%), Rouge-L 0.605 (-0.8%), latency p50 110ms
- Int8 baseline: EM 0.71 (-1.4%)
- Safety flags: small increase for PTQ variants (from 3% -> 4.2% flagged) — need to run more checks

Observations / Notes:
- PTQ gives the biggest latency/cost wins but shows larger drop on long-context QA (prod-qa-200) — see detailed evals in ./evals/2026-03-11/qa.csv
- QAT reduced the quality gap substantially for short instructions; seems to help with retrieval-style prompts if calibration dataset includes R-Examples
- Act-order tweak recovered ~0.5% EM over baseline PTQ; worth baking into conversion script if reproducible
- One noisy run where PTQ had EM 0.68 — suspected batchseed/ordering; re-run with fixed RNG

Immediate todos (short):
- [ ] Re-run PTQ-4c-clip3 with fixed RNG and seed=42 (Jordan)
- [ ] Run extended safety evals (toxicity + jailbreak suite) on all variants (Asha) — high priority before dev rollout
- [ ] Add 1k calibration examples targeted at retrieval prompts and re-run QAT with 5k steps (Liam + Jordan)
- [ ] Capture p95 cost numbers on dedicated infra (P4d vs g5.xlarge) for cost model (Jordan)

Longer-term / followups:
- If QAT at 5k steps closes gap to <1% EM, consider recommending QAT for customer-managed private deployments where training budget is ok.
- Explore mixed-precision path: keep KV cache in 8-bit, attention matmul in 4-bit — prototype in runtime branch.
- Add per-prompt failure logging to Console (product-hosted-api feature request) so we can track regressions at rollout time.

Open questions / risks:
- Does clipping=3.0 generalize across models? Need to test on 13B family.
- Safety regression: random seeds seemed to affect hallucination rate. Is this quant sensitivity or sampling variance?
- Runtime compatibility: act-order conversion requires slight model-format change; will it break Dedicated/Private loader? File a compatibility ticket if we adopt.

Notes to self:
- Use smaller eval shards for fast iteration (100 examples) before full runs. Keep baseline runs reproducible with seed files in runs/seed-files/
- Save all conversion logs: ./runs/<tag>/convert.log — helpful when debugging clipping troubleshoot

Links / refs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/quant-eval-run-2026-03
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-quant-pr-78
- Jira: JIRA-ML-412 (quantification task), JIRA-ML-419 (safety evaluation)

End of scratchpad — will clean up and move stable notes to a PR/Confluence when we have reproducible numbers.
